result.explanation: Most likely board-side: its XRCE transport or buffer sent a zero-filled datagram 108 ms after a valid CREATE_CLIENT. The agent only reacted to it. Wire capture is needed to exclude the host side.

hypotheses.claim: The board's XRCE UDP transport or buffer sent a zero-filled datagram, then kept re-sending a static 13-byte buffer.
hypotheses.because: Valid create at line 5, then 36 zero bytes at line 11, then identical 13-byte packets every 0.1 s. This looks like a stale or uninitialised buffer.

hypotheses.claim: The agent or host receive path mangled or misparsed a valid datagram.
hypotheses.because: The agent parsed line 5 correctly. The zero payload is consistent with its handling, and the delete follows by design. Not excluded without a capture.

hypotheses.claim: Packet corruption or loss on the link caused the bad datagram.
hypotheses.because: A full 36-byte all-zero datagram is unlikely from corruption, and the earlier packets passed. No capture to confirm.

hypotheses.claim: The agent port argument 457879 is out of range and wraps to 64663.
hypotheses.because: Line 1 gives 457879 but line 2 shows 64663, and the board connected on the first packet. The port wrap is a config smell, not the cause of the zero packet.

events.why: Port wraps modulo 65536 but the session still opens. Worth fixing.

steps.label: Read the report and earlier results

result.headline: Board sent 36 zero bytes after a valid create; agent closed the session and the board kept resending a 13-byte packet.
result.explanation: The board's Tx buffer is correct at sendto, but zeros reach the wire. The fault is below the XRCE layer, in the board's UDP/Ethernet path. D-cache and DMA buffer coherence is the leading candidate; this is not confirmed.

evidence.shows: The first datagram is a valid CREATE_CLIENT. The board can send correct data.
The next datagram is 36 bytes of zeros, with client_key 0x2A2ED975 already established.
The agent deletes the session 123 ms after it was created (line 6 at .431336, line 13 at .539573). This is an effect of the zero payload.
After the zero packet the board sends the same 13 bytes about every 0.1 s. Lines 18 to 34 show this pattern, and the board is not a working node.

checked.check: Read the full 34-line log for the order of events and the payloads.
checked.result: Valid create at line 5, session established at line 7, 36 zero bytes at line 11, delete at line 13, then identical 13-byte packets from line 18.

checked.check: Engineer capture on the agent host, compared with the board's Tx buffer at sendto.
checked.result: The Tx buffer holds the right XRCE bytes at sendto, but tcpdump shows 36 zero bytes on the wire. D-cache is enabled.
checked.about: h2 (agent and host receive path) and h3 (network corruption)

checked.result: No earlier cases are in the workspace.

effects.why: The agent handled the bad datagram and closed the session.

effects.quote: [1707258509.539636] warning  | Root.cpp           | create_client            | invalid client key     | client_key: 0x00000000
effects.why: This is the agent's reaction to the zero payload. Key 0 is invalid.

effects.quote: [1707258509.643521] debug    | UDPv4AgentLinux.cpp | recv_message             | [==>> UDP <<==]        | client_key: 0x00000000, len: 13, data:
effects.why: The board keeps sending after the session is gone. This is the follow-on behavior, not a cause.

next_action.action: Make the Ethernet Tx buffers and descriptors non-cacheable, or clean the D-cache before transmit, then retest.
next_action.why: This tests whether D-cache and DMA incoherence causes the wire to carry zeros while the Tx buffer is correct.
how: Place the lwIP/Ethernet Tx buffers and descriptors in a region marked non-cacheable by the MPU, or in D2 SRAM with the MPU configured.
Alternatively call SCB_CleanDCache_by_Addr on the Tx buffer before the sendto/DMA kick.
As a quick test only, disable the D-cache with SCB_DisableDCache() and rerun the agent capture.

outcomes.label: Wire now carries the correct bytes
outcomes.means: Cache and DMA coherence is the cause. Fix it in the MPU or cache maintenance configuration.

outcomes.label: Wire still shows 36 zero bytes
outcomes.means: Cache is not the cause. Look at the Ethernet driver, the DMA descriptors, or lwIP pbuf handling.

unknowns: It is not known which layer zeroes the data: cache, DMA descriptor, driver or pbuf.
The log does not show how the 13-byte packet is generated or why it repeats.

hypotheses.claim: The board's UDP/Ethernet path, most likely D-cache and DMA coherence, sends zeros although the Tx buffer is correct.
hypotheses.because: Valid bytes at sendto but 36 zero bytes on the wire, with D-cache enabled. The agent and network are cleared by the capture.

hypotheses.claim: The agent or host receive path mangled or misparsed a valid datagram.
hypotheses.because: tcpdump on the agent host shows 36 zero bytes on the wire, so the zeros existed before the agent received them.

hypotheses.claim: Packet corruption or loss on the link caused the bad datagram.
hypotheses.because: The zeros are on the wire at the agent host, and the engineer reports the board or its transport sent them. A whole datagram of zeros is not corruption.

hypotheses.claim: The agent port argument 457879 is out of range and wraps to 64663.
hypotheses.because: The board connected on the first packet, so the port wrap is a config smell and not the cause of the zero packet.

result.reuse_when: STM32H7 (Cortex-M7) with micro-ROS XRCE over UDP/lwIP and Ethernet DMA, D-cache enabled, with Tx buffers or descriptors in cacheable RAM. Signature: valid first create, then an all-zero datagram, then a repeated static packet.

close.cause: D-cache not cleaned before the Ethernet DMA sent the Tx buffer: the DMA read stale memory and sent zeros, so the agent dropped the session.
close.fix: Clean the D-cache over the Tx buffer (cache-line aligned) before each send, or put the Ethernet buffers in a non-cacheable MPU region.
close.applies_when: STM32H7/F7 with D-cache enabled and Ethernet DMA; packets correct in the CPU's buffer but zero on the wire.
